invariants: A Claim is a value, not a guard: dropping it does nothing on the server.
claim returns Ok(None) when the server returns SQL NULL (nothing claimable) - never an error.

Unit tests in this file cover ONLY Claim::from_json and RenewStatus::parse (pure logic): a full payload decodes and raw equals the payload; a missing field is Protocol; a malformed uuid is Protocol; all five statuses parse and an unknown one is Protocol.
responsibilities: Claim::from_json decodes the claim payload: string fields via as_str, uuid fields via as_str + Uuid::parse_str, recipe cloned from the payload; every missing or mistyped field is a Protocol error naming the field. raw is a clone of the WHOLE payload (there is no 'raw' key).
WorkerApi methods call PgSession's public call_* helpers with the literal SELECT strings in the signature - never run_query (private) and never a bare function name without SELECT.

Parameters are always passed as references: &[&attempt_id, &attempt_token, ...]. Option parameters (manifest, usage, progress_signal) are passed as the Option itself (&manifest, &progress_signal) so None becomes SQL NULL - never unwrap_or a default.

renew_status first probes with call_bool and the literal probe select in the signature; on the typed path it maps the returned text through RenewStatus::parse; on the fallback path it calls renew() and maps true -> Renewed, false -> LeaseExpired.
publish probes publish_with_cause ONLY when outcome is "failed" and failure_cause is Some; otherwise it calls publish directly.
RenewStatus::parse accepts exactly the five statuses and rejects anything else as Protocol.
summary: The worker surface: Claim (the lease), RenewStatus, and WorkerApi - typed calls over forge_coding_worker_api, one function per method, mirroring WorkerDB's worker role.
